newsitem.title: USA: Carnival holders to offer 21.6 mln shrs.
newsitem.headline: Carnival holders to offer 21.6 mln shrs.

text.p: Cruise line operator Carnival Corp said on Friday some shareholders planned to offer a total of 21.6 million Class A common shares in a public offering.

The company said it filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on behalf of Ted Arison, The New World Symphony Supporting Foundation Inc and other entities related to Arison.
Arison was selling his shares for estate planning and other related purposes, the company said.

The offering would be made in the United States and internationally and Arison would grant the underwriters over-allotment options to purchase up to 3.24 million shares of Carnival's class A common stock, the company said.
Carnival said it would receive no profit from the sale.

If the offering was completed, Arison family members would beneficially own 48.2 percent of the outstanding capital stock of the company, giving the family about 70.4 percent voting control over the company.
The managing underwriters were Goldman, Sachs & Co, Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, Lehman Brothers and Merrill Lynch & Co.
The company said it planned to start the public offering as soon as the registration statement became effective.
